context: A police archivist guides a uni student through old records
purpose: Teach: 東西/南北/に際して/にわたり/東海/本土/中期/大和

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: ようこそ。閲覧に際して、いくつかご留意いただきたい点があります。
lines.en: Welcome. Before viewing, there are a few things I'd like you to keep in mind.
lines.style: Formal, measured tone with archival gravity and gentle authority.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、よろしくお願いします。大和朝廷の頃の古い資料を探しているんですが。
lines.en: Yes, thank you. I'm looking for old materials from around the Yamato court period.
lines.style: Polite student register, slightly nervous but genuinely curious throughout.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: ああ、それでしたらここでは難しいですね。当館の所蔵は江戸中期以降のものに限られていまして。
lines.en: Ah, in that case it'll be difficult here. Our holdings are limited to materials from mid-Edo onward.
lines.style: Patient correction, professional clarification with quiet pride in collection.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: そうですか…ええと、では時代を変えて、東海地方の治安史でも大丈夫ですか?
lines.en: I see... um, then changing the era, would Tokai-region public-order history be okay?
lines.style: Quickly recalibrating, mildly disappointed but adapting on the spot.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: ええ、その辺なら豊富ですよ。江戸後期から明治初期までの長きにわたり、東西の街道沿いに事件が集中していまして。
lines.en: Yes, that area we have plenty of. Over a long stretch from late Edo through early Meiji, incidents were concentrated along the east-west highways.
lines.style: Warming up, sharing expert knowledge with growing enthusiasm and detail.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 南北の往来はどうだったんですか?本土の山間部を抜ける裏道なんかの記録も残っていますか?
lines.en: What about north-south travel? Are there records of back routes cutting through the mainland mountains?
lines.style: Academic curiosity sharpening into focus, leaning into the new angle.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 山越えの古文書も何点かあったはずです。ただ私も先月人事異動で来たばかりでして。
lines.en: There should be several old documents on the mountain crossings. Though I only transferred here last month.
lines.style: Apologetic honesty, humble admission of limits despite the uniform.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: あ、そうだったんですね。お忙しいところ、本当にすみません。
lines.en: Oh, I see. I'm really sorry to trouble you when you're so busy.
lines.style: Grateful and accommodating, eager not to be a burden on staff.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: いえいえ、では閲覧申請のテンプレートをお渡ししますので、ご記入をお願いします。
lines.en: Not at all. Then I'll hand you the viewing request template, so please fill it in.
lines.style: Returning to procedural mode, kind but firm about bureaucratic steps.
